messages:
Incident-Bot: :warning: Automatic alert: token-serving latency spike detected across select KV shards
Incident-Bot: p95=1.82s (SLO=1.2s), p99=3.7s. Streaming stalls and tail latency windows increasing.

Kai: I'm on call. Pulling traces and kv metrics now.

Kai: @Nina can you open the fragmentation + allocator dashboards? I want to see free segment counts and any recent allocator rollouts.

Nina: grabbing dashboards -> https://dashboards.prod/kv/frag-and-alloc
Nina: quick read: shard-4 and shard-10 showing free_segments <= 4, heavy decode ops vs prefill (decodes ~5.2k, prefills ~180 in 15m). Eviction spikes correlated with p99 windows.

DevOps-Bot: recent infra event: cache-allocator v2.15 deployed cluster-wide at 02:58Z (canary at 02:51Z). No other infra changes.

Rafael: tail logs snippet from streaming-router:
Rafael: ```
2026-03-15T02:59:20Z shard=4 req=Zx8a stall_ms=3100 decode_ms=2700 prefill_hit=false
2026-03-15T03:00:01Z shard=10 req=Yp7b stall_ms=4200 decode_ms=3800 prefill_hit=false
```

Priya: running immediate metrics pull for shards 4,10 (15m window):
Priya: ```
# curl 'https://metrics.api/kv?shards=4,10&window=15m' | jq '.shard_metrics'
# result (summarized)
shard-4: evictions=3880 prefills=170 decodes=5200 free_segments=3
shard-10: evictions=3715 prefills=150 decodes=4950 free_segments=4
```

Kai: pattern fits allocator change increasing fragmentation -> more evictions, prefill starving -> decode-heavy requests bypass cache and cause stalls. Impacting streaming-heavy customers (SearchPro and QuickChat).

Support-Lead: Support reports increased p95 and customer-visible retries for SearchPro. They've opened SEV tickets; customers notified that we're investigating.

Kai: Proposed immediate mitigations (short-term):
1) fast rollback of cache-allocator to previous version on affected nodes
2) enable targeted forced prefill for top 200 hot prefixes on shards 4/10 for 15m
3) lower eviction aggressiveness (soft throttle) for 10m
4) admission-control: temporarily limit concurrent long streaming sessions (>1800 tokens) for 10m

Nina: rollback path is ready. Note: rollback will not instantly defragment existing fragmentation; it should stop adding churn. We should start a controlled compaction after rollback stabilizes.

DevOps-Bot: initiating rollback -> cache-allocator v2.14 applied to canary pool on shard-4 at 03:07:12Z.

Priya: metrics 2m after rollback: evictions dropping (~70% reduction on canary), decodes slowly declining. Prefills still low for non-top prefixes.

Rafael: scheduling a rate-limited compaction job (low CPU footprint):
Rafael: ```
POST /ops/compaction?shards=4,10&workers=2&rate=0.15
# returned job_id=compaction-3625001234
```

Nina: also enabling targeted forced prefill for top-200 prefixes at 03:10:05Z. This should bump prefill hits for hottest keys and reduce decode work.

Incident-Bot: Action summary: rollback started, compaction job enqueued, forced_prefill enabled, eviction throttle applied, admission control enabled.

Priya: 5m check: p95 reduced from 1.82s -> 1.08s, p99 3.7s -> 1.9s. Evictions on shard-4 down from ~3800 to ~980 in last 5m window. Free_segments rising slowly (3->9).

Support-Lead: Customer update sent: SearchPro and QuickChat notified of mitigations and expected improvements. Will send another update in 30m.

Rafael: compaction progress: 22% complete after 7m, CPU impact within acceptable thresholds (avg CPU for compactor ~18%).

Kai: good signals. Keep monitoring for at least 30m before lifting admission controls. If p99 creeps above 2.5s, we'll re-evaluate and consider traffic shuffles.

Nina: note for follow-up: allocator v2.15 introduced a placement behavior that prefers many small allocations which increases fragmentation under long-lived streaming workloads. Need postmortem and safety gate for canary when free_segments < threshold.

Priya: 20m update: compaction at 81%, free_segments now 28 on shard-4, 25 on shard-10. p95 0.99s, p99 1.4s. Decodes back to near-baseline.

Rafael: sample post-mit logs showing warm cache hits after forced prefill:
Rafael: ```
2026-03-15T03:24:42Z shard=4 req=Lm9c stall_ms=880 decode_ms=120 prefill_hit=true
2026-03-15T03:24:48Z shard=10 req=Qw3d stall_ms=940 decode_ms=150 prefill_hit=true
```

Kai: moving incident to MONITORING. Nina will take the active handoff and run the follow-up analysis.

Nina: accepting handoff. I'll keep the dashboards watched for the next hour, validate compaction completed, and ensure no memory/OOM regressions. I'll also create the RCA ticket and coordinate postmortem writing.

Support-Lead: closing customer communication loop: follow-up note will include timeline, mitigations, and next-steps from engineering.

Incident-Bot: UPDATE: 3625003234: p95=1.01s, p99=1.42s. Incident state: MONITORING.

Rafael: created ticket ops/kv-allocator-frag-3625 with timeline and mitigation steps. Assigned to infra team to add allocator safety checks and schedule allocator behavior tests under long-lived stream load.

Kai: quick list of action items to include in postmortem:
- root cause: allocator v2.15 allocation pattern causing fragmentation under long-lived streams
- short-term: rollback + compaction + forced prefill + eviction throttle + admission control
- long-term: allocator safety gates, background compaction in maintenance windows, smarter prefill heuristics, better canary health signals (free_segments metric), and load-tested allocator rollout plan

Nina: I'll draft the postmortem and link customer impact stats. Good work all.

Support-Lead: Thanks team. I'll update customers when the postmortem is published.

Incident-Bot: Postmortem stub: https://pm.redwood/3625001234-kv-frag-incident

Kai: thanks everyone. If anything regresses, please page @oncall.
